newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends higher ahead of USDA export data.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends higher ahead of USDA export data.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures ended slightly firmer despite expectations for a weak shipment showing in Thursday's export and sales report, floor sources said.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture will release its data Thursday at 0830 EST. Market sources expect shipments only around 150,000 480-lb bales, since the benchmark May contract hit a recent high of 76.45 cents during the week.
May cotton closed up 0.48 to 75.26 cents per pound, having ranged from 75.44 to 74.95 cents. Spot March went out 0.45 firmer at 73.50 cents.
Volume was estimated at only 5,000 lots, down from Tuesday's official 15,621 lots.
Market sources expect continued caution in the market ahead of several key reports. The USDA will issue its monthly supply and demand data March 11.

Several analysts expect the USDA to raise its export estimate to as much as 6.8 million bales for the 1996/97 marketing year, while others said the current rate of weekly shipments will not even total the current 6.5 million bale estimate.
The USDA will release its first, widely-watched estimate of planted cotton area for 1997/98, on March 31.
